system.title: Regime-tested, reliability-measured estimation of regional excitability in a whole-brain MPR model with a noise-aware PINN (r14)

planets.label: Regional excitabilities of a whole-brain MPR model from one subject, with the regime decided by the data
planets.detail: Estimate G and the regional excitabilities eta_i of an MPR whole-brain model from one subject's resting-state fMRI, decide the regime from the data, measure reliability and reconstruct regional states.

evidence.quote: The aim is to estimate the global coupling $G$ and the regional excitabilities $\eta_i$ of an MPR whole-brain model

planets.label: Resting-state fMRI dynamics
planets.detail: Bistable and monostable configurations fitted to the same real data, read against a linear network floor.

evidence.quote: fitted to the same real data by forward stochastic simulation

planets.label: Physics-informed neural networks with a noise forcing
planets.detail: A PINN whose V equation carries a zero-mean Fourier forcing with a Gaussian prior tied to the fixed noise level.

evidence.quote: reconstruct the regional states with a noise-aware PINN

planets.label: Single-subject resting-state fMRI
planets.detail: Any dataset; H1 sets the number of volumes and hence the dataset, not tied to 1000BRAINS.

evidence.quote: one subject of a resting-state dataset, parcellated into $N$ regions, with $T$ volumes at repetition time TR

planets.label: Regime-assumed estimates of regional excitability of unknown reliability
planets.detail: The regime is fixed before fitting and FC alone does not determine eta_i, so estimates inherit an untested regime and their test-retest reliability is unknown for the MPR.

evidence.quote: Regime-assumed estimates of regional excitabilities $\eta_i$, of unknown reliability, in whole-brain MPR models fitted to single-subject resting-state fMRI

planets.label: Bistable against monostable configuration of one biophysical model on real resting-state fMRI
planets.detail: The two configurations of the same MPR model are compared on the same data after a synthetic test of discriminability; to the authors' knowledge no earlier study does this.

evidence.quote: no study has compared a bistable and a monostable configuration of the same biophysical neural mass model on real resting-state fMRI

planets.label: Parameter inference for brain network models
planets.detail: Estimation of the parameters of a connectome-based model from neuroimaging data.

evidence.quote: Every parameter that is not estimated is fixed and declared.

planets.label: Identifiability gate on synthetic data
planets.detail: Before any real fit, synthetic BOLD of both configurations, preprocessed as the real data, decides which scale-free statistics identify the regime and recover G and eta_i, and whether free eta_i or the map is the target.

evidence.quote: H1 decides the estimation target, the free $\eta_i$ when they are recovered with statistics that survive the pre

planets.label: Reliability measured, not assumed
planets.detail: Reliability of G and eta_i across seeds, initial values and sessions, with an intraclass correlation across sessions.

evidence.quote: the reliability of the estimates is measured across seeds, initial values and sessions (H3)

planets.label: Regime decided by the data along a noise grid
planets.detail: Bistable and monostable configurations fitted to the same data with a sweep and CMA-ES, compared on held-out BOLD statistics, with a linear model as lower reference.

evidence.quote: the bistable and the monostable configuration are fitted to the same real data by forward stochastic simulation

planets.label: Noise-aware PINN as transversal estimator and reconstructor of slow regional states
planets.detail: The PINN is one estimator among those compared; its specific role is to reconstruct which state each region occupies. Its noise forcing term is owed in r13.

evidence.quote: its specific role is to reconstruct which state each region occupies over time

planets.label: Zero-mean noise forcing tied to the noise level
planets.detail: A per-region Fourier forcing starting at k=1, so it cannot absorb eta_i, with a Gaussian prior whose variance follows from the fixed noise level.

evidence.quote: The sum starts at $k=1$, so $u_i$ has zero mean over the window

planets.label: FC fit read against ceilings and a linear floor
planets.detail: Success read against seed and session ceilings; bistable and monostable fits read against a linear network floor.

evidence.quote: Success is read against the ceilings of Section 6

planets.label: Parameters interpreted only if identifiable
planets.detail: Expected, not yet measured: parameters are interpreted only after synthetic recovery and convergence across seeds and sessions.

evidence.quote: The parameters are called interpretable when three conditions hold.

pillars.label: Regime decided by the data
pillars.detail: Fit the bistable and the monostable configuration of the same MPR model to the same data and decide the regime from held-out dynamic statistics, against a linear floor, along a noise grid

pillars.label: Identifiability before any real fit
pillars.detail: Establish on synthetic data, before any real fit, which BOLD statistics identify the regime and recover G and eta_i, using functional and spatio-temporal features

pillars.label: Reliability measured, not assumed
pillars.detail: Measure the reliability of G and eta_i across seeds, initial values and sessions of the same subject, instead of assuming it

pillars.label: Noise-aware PINN as transversal estimator
pillars.detail: A PINN with a noise forcing term, needed in both regimes, that estimates the parameters and reconstructs the hidden trajectories r_i(t), V_i(t) and the regional states lasting long enough for BOLD to resolve

hypotheses.statement: On synthetic BOLD of both configurations, preprocessed as the real data (detrending, GSR), FC, FCD and scale-free regional statistics identify the regime and recover $G$ and free $\eta_i$, or else the map $\eta_0+a\,m_i$, within the pilot tolerance, across the $\sigma_\xi$ grid

On real single-subject BOLD, bistable and monostable fits differ in held-out dynamic statistics by more than seed and, when available, session variability, read against a linear floor and reported along the $\sigma_\xi$ grid

Repeated fits with different seeds, initial values and, when available, a second session give the same $G$ and $\eta_i$ within their spread, with the mapped parametrisation $\eta_i=\eta_0+a\,m_i$ as comparison

A noise-aware PINN recovers on synthetic data the fraction of time each region spends in each state, and on real data its estimates give an FC no worse than sweep and CMA-ES under a declared simulation budget
